Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

a adjective

the indefinite article

also an, a certain

classical

Quint. 1.4.19: noster sermō articulōs nōn dēsīderat

nōmen sine articulō

Latin has no article

no word: the noun alone

English “a” is not translated: “a dog was carrying a piece of meat across a river” is canis per flūmen carnem cum ferret (Phaedr. 1.4.2).

Other words

  • quīdam, quaedam, quoddam — a, a certain (known to the speaker, not named)

    indefinite adjective; as a pronoun quīdam, quaedam, quiddam · also used · classical · Phaedr. 2.5.1: est ardaliōnum quaedam Rōmae nātiō

    The “a” of a story, or of someone one has in mind: “a man I know”. See “someone”.

  • ūnus, ūna, ūnum — a, one (a single one)

    numeral adjective; genitive ūnīus, dative ūnī · also used · classical · Vulg. Jo. 6.9: Est puer ūnus hīc

    Where English “a” means “one”.

Examples

  • canis per flūmen carnem cum ferret natāns

    a dog was swimming across a river with a piece of meatPhaedr. 1.4.2

  • est ardaliōnum quaedam Rōmae nātiō

    there is at Rome a tribe of busybodiesPhaedr. 2.5.1

  • Est puer ūnus hīc quī habet quīnque pānēs hordeāceōs et duōs piscēs

    There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fishVulg. Jo. 6.9

See also the, someone, certain.
